study_identification_part.si3_author_journal_year: Yu et al., Human Brain Mapping, 2024
study_identification_part.si4_title: Behavioral and brain morphological changes before and after hemispherotomy

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract and introduction clearly state the study's aims: to investigate pre-to-post surgical changes in gray matter volume (GMV) and their relationships with behavioral scores in pediatric hemispherotomy patients, and to control developmental effects using a normative modeling approach. This addresses both the research questions and explicitly describes the purpose of applying normative modeling (adjusting for development to enable individual-level comparisons and prediction).
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "we systematically investigated changes in gray matter volume (GMV) before and after surgery and further analyzed their relationships with behavioral scores... To control for the dramatic developmental effect during this stage, age-adjusted GMV... was derived... using a normative modeling approach with an age-matched reference cohort of 2115 healthy children."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: For the newly built normative model, the paper specifies the eligibility (healthy children aged 0.3–13.0 years; max 100 per half-year bin; single highest-quality scan per subject), image quality and completeness standards (exclude poor-quality images or processing failures), and reports the final sample size (2115) with reasons for exclusion (n=228 due to poor quality or processing failure). It also cites original data sources.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "we included T1-weighted images from all healthy children aged between 0.3 and 13.0 years across these datasets, with a maximum of 100 subjects for a half-year interval... For children with multiple T1-weighted images, only the image of the highest quality was used... Among these images, 228 were excluded due to poor image quality or image processing failure... VBM processing was then applied to the remaining 2115 children..."
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.location: Yu2024.pdf.md:110-118; HBM-45-e70020-s001.docx.md:lines under 'The inclusion criteria of T1-weighted images'

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age and sex are explicitly included as covariates in the voxelwise normative model. However, despite multi-dataset sourcing, there is no description of site-effect handling (e.g., site covariate, ComBat, or hierarchical modeling).
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "Age and sex were included as covariates in the model. For each voxel, Gaussian process regression was applied... yielding a Z score representing the patient's derivation from the age- and sex-matched healthy norm."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: Data sources of the healthy reference cohort are listed by name (11 MRI datasets) and references are provided, satisfying specification of source for an originally built model.
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "the healthy subjects used for normative model estimation were from 11 MRI datasets, including the Autism Brain Imaging Data Exchange..., the UNC/UMN Baby Connectome Project..., ... the Pediatric Imaging, Neurocognition, and Genetics..., and the Pixar Dataset..."

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: This item applies only when the reference cohort was primarily collected in this study. The reference cohort comprises secondary data from existing datasets; per guide, answer NA.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: Reference cohort drawn from existing datasets (ABIDE, BCP, HCPD, IBIS, PING, etc.).

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is described: VBM using SPM12, creation of symmetric template, longitudinal registration, bias correction, tissue segmentation, spatial normalization, modulation, smoothing, masking of the operated hemisphere, and visual QC.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "We then carried out voxel-based morphometry (VBM) analyses using SPM12... Longitudinal VBM processing included... average image... bias-corrected and segmented... registered to the symmetric template... modulated... smoothed with an 8-mm FWHM Gaussian kernel... The resultant images of each step were carefully checked by visual inspection."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: For a newly built model, internal validation would involve partitioning within the healthy reference cohort (e.g., CV, hold-out). The methods describe training on all 2115 healthy children and testing on patients, but no cross-validation or hold-out within the healthy cohort is reported.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "The GMV images of the 2115 healthy children and our pediatric hemispherotomy patients were used as the training and testing data, respectively." (no mention of CV/hold-out within healthy cohort)

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: No application of the normative model to an independent external healthy dataset is described. The model is trained on healthy children and applied to patients.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: No statement of external validation on independent healthy data; only application to patient cohort is described.

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is specified: voxelwise Gaussian process regression using PCNtoolkit, with software and versions (Python 3.8.13; PCNtoolkit 0.26), covariates (age, sex), and output (Z scores).
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "The voxelwise GMV normative modeling procedure was then applied using Python 3.8.13 and PCNtoolkit (0.26)... Age and sex were included as covariates... For each voxel, Gaussian process regression was applied... yielding a Z score..."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: No quantitative metrics of model fit/calibration on the reference cohort (e.g., explained variance, prediction error, coverage) are reported.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: No performance metrics reported for the normative fit on the healthy cohort.

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: No data partitioning of the healthy reference cohort is performed; per guide, when no partitioning is used, answer NA.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: Training used the full healthy cohort without splits; no train/validation/test partitions within healthy data are described.

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Software and library versions for normative modeling are provided (Python 3.8.13; PCNtoolkit 0.26). However, code/trained model availability and data access conditions beyond citations are not stated.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "...applied using Python 3.8.13 and PCNtoolkit (0.26)." (no mention of code or model availability)

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: For the primary clinical cohort, the study specifies patient eligibility/inclusion criteria, reports image quality screening with reasons for exclusion (processing failure due to poor quality), and provides final sample sizes.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "The patient inclusion criteria were as follows: (1) underwent peri-insular hemispherotomy between 2016 and 2021... (2) were at least half a year old... (3) had available pre- and postoperative MRI images; and (4) no other brain surgery... Initially, 74 patients met these criteria, but the image processing procedures failed for 17 of them due to the poor quality of either pre- or postoperative MRI images... Finally, 29... left and 28... right hemispherotomy patients were included."

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses relate imaging deviation scores to behavioral outcomes and prediction but do not report inclusion of clinical covariates beyond demographics (e.g., medication, illness duration, symptom severity) in these models.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: No description of adjusting for medication status, illness duration, or other clinical covariates in the deviation score analyses.

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: Primary clinical cohort data collection site and period are specified, and MRI acquisition protocol details (vendor, field strength, sequence parameters) are provided.
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text:
"Pediatric patients... were recruited... between 2016 and 2021 at the Pediatric Epilepsy Center, Peking University First Hospital." 
"High-quality MRI was acquired before and after the surgery using a Philips Achieva 3T scanner... All T1-weighted scans used the same MPRAGE sequence with the following parameters..."

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample sizes are reported and the text states demographic and clinical information are provided in Table 1, but detailed demographics and clinical characteristics are not enumerated in the extracted text body.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: "Finally, 29... left and 28... right hemispherotomy patients were included... Demographic and clinical information is listed in Table 1."

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: The clinical assessment measure (Griffiths Scales of Child Development, 3rd ed.) is specified, domains are listed, and assessment timing is described.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: "The Griffiths Scales of Child Development (3rd edition, Griffiths III)... includes five domains... The evaluation was usually performed on the same day as the MRI."

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The meaning and direction of the deviation scores (age- and sex-adjusted GMV Z-scores) are explained, and clinical implications are discussed (associations with behavioral improvement and predictive potential). However, no quantitative thresholds for categorization (e.g., |Z| > 1.96) are provided.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text:
"The age-adjusted GMV values (i.e., Z scores) represent the patient's deviation from the age- and sex-matched norm: negative and positive values indicate a trend of GM shrinkage and expansion, respectively." 
"...a greater GMV decrease was associated with greater behavioral improvement in right hemispherotomy patients."
